Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua to SNUB Wembley and take place on a FRIDAY in New York to avoid clash with NFL: Date set with contracts signed as Britain's biggest fight goes abroad... and fans back home could face a VERY late night
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are understood to have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City, bringing an end to years of negotiations over the biggest all-British heavyweight fight of the modern era.

Fury took to social media on Tuesday morning to tease the announcement, telling his followers that the fight was on the verge of being publicised. He said: 'Big news being dropped very, very soon. A big fight on the horizon. It's the one you've all been waiting for. It's about to be announced imminently so stay tuned!'.

Daily Mail Sport understands that the final details were thrashed out at a meeting earlier this week, with the venue the main outstanding issue. It's believed plans are now being put in place for the official announcement, which is expected to take place at an 'iconic' British landmark at the start of next week.

While the timing of the fight has not been confirmed, the news will raise fears that fans wanting to watch back home are likely to face a very late night - with New York five hours behind the UK.

Those familiar with the discussions say Joshua and his promoter Eddie Hearn continued to push for the fight to take place in the UK, with Fury also keen on a homecoming event.

However, Hearn - who recently revealed it was written into AJ’s contract that the fight had to be staged in Britain - has told Daily Mail Sport that no agreement has yet been reached, despite reports to the contrary.

'We are in constant communication with Turki (Alalshikh, Saudi boxing chief) but as of yet there is no agreement to any variation within the contract,' he said.

It is understood that Anthony Joshua (left) and Tyson Fury (right) have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City

Others close to the discussions say Alalshikh’s position was that the fight could be staged in the UK if the financial case stacked up and the figures could be demonstrated.

But with that case ultimately unable to be made, the decision has been taken to move the blockbuster to New York and the iconic Madison Square Garden - the scene of Joshua’s shock defeat by Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019.

The fight is expected to take place on a Friday night, according to those briefed on the plans, in an attempt to avoid clashes with major American sporting events and maximise its exposure in the US.

It remains unclear, however, whether the main event will take place at a time convenient for British boxing fans.

The final pieces are now being put in place for the official announcement, with the relevant parties due to meet in the coming days to organise the launch press conference.

That is expected to take place before the end of August.

The fight is said to be taking in New York and the iconic Madison Square Garden - where Joshua previously suffered his shock defeat by Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019

Turki Alalshikh (above), who is helping bankroll the fight, had left the door open to staging the event in Britain, but made it clear that the numbers had to work

Spencer Brown, Fury's manager, said several weeks ago that the announcement would be made at an iconic British landmark, adding that it would be 'like no announcement' fans have ever seen before and claiming they 'don't want to miss it'.

Hearn has also previously told Daily Mail Sport that the announcement press conference would take place before the end of the month and would be timed around Joshua's return from holiday.

The roots of Joshua-Fury go back to the beginning of the 2010s, when both men were establishing themselves as Britain's leading heavyweight prospects.

Joshua won Olympic gold at London 2012 before turning professional, while Fury had already made his professional debut in 2008 and was building an unbeaten record of his own.

For years, the prospect of the two eventually meeting was one of British boxing's biggest talking points.

Anthony Joshua has his hand raised following victory over Kristian Prenga on July 25

However, result didn't come without drama as he was knocked down in the first 20 seconds

Fury's victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 transformed him into a world heavyweight champion, while Joshua was rapidly moving towards the same position.

Joshua won the IBF heavyweight title by beating Charles Martin in 2016 and subsequently added the WBA and IBO belts.

By 2017, the possibility of an undisputed Joshua-Fury fight had become a genuine objective rather than simply a dream matchup.

But the negotiations repeatedly failed.

The biggest opportunity came in 2021, when Joshua and Fury appeared to be moving towards a two-fight agreement. A deal was publicly discussed, but the proposed fight ultimately collapsed after Fury became obligated to face Deontay Wilder following an arbitration ruling.

Fury subsequently fought Wilder for a third time, while Joshua moved towards his own defining bouts.

Joshua then suffered back-to-back defeats against Oleksandr Usyk, losing his WBA, IBF and WBO titles in 2021 before being beaten again in their 2022 rematch.

The sport then appeared to get another opportunity to make Joshua-Fury. In late 2022, negotiations accelerated dramatically, with both camps discussing a proposed fight in December.

Fury took on Mariusz Wach at the Max Muay Thai Stadium, Pattaya, Thailand on July 24

Fury emerged victorious and had been expected ringside for AJ's fight with Prenga

A deal again failed to materialise.

Fury instead moved on to other opponents, while Joshua continued his rebuilding process following the Usyk defeats.

The arrival of Alalshikh and the expansion of major boxing events in Saudi Arabia created a new route to making the fight.

Now, after years of failed negotiations and multiple points at which the fight appeared close before falling apart, the contracts have finally been signed.

Joshua-Fury is no longer a fight being negotiated.

It is happening.

November 20. Madison Square Garden.

Sports.title: England's 'brave new dawn' is nothing but a return to the past, procrastination disguised as progress under a skipper lacking tactical nous and a coach tainted by Bazball's bombast, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
England's 'brave new dawn' is nothing but a return to the past, procrastination disguised as progress under a skipper lacking tactical nous and a coach tainted by Bazball's bombast, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

It has come to something when an England team who arrived in Australia in November with high hopes of winning back the Ashes begin a home series against lowly Pakistan with ridicule breathing down their neck.

England have had a decent stab at portraying Wednesday's first Test at Headingley as a fresh dawn – and haven’t we had a few of those. But the return as captain on his home ground of Joe Root and the presence of Marcus Trescothick as stand-in coach feels not so much a brave new world as a relic from the past. It is procrastination disguised as progress.

Until Stephen Fleming takes over in time for the winter series in South Africa, England will be treading water. Victory over a Pakistan team ranked seventh in the world will do little more than keep Root’s team afloat. Defeat, and they could very well go under.

It does not bear thinking about, especially since Australia’s humiliation by Bangladesh in Darwin has, briefly, given them some material for the never-ending battle of Ashes banter.

The absence of Fleming, though, has done little to dispel the sense that England have wasted the past few months. Instead of being sacked after the Ashes, as might easily have happened in another era, Brendon McCullum was allowed to carry on into the summer, at which point Ben Stokes’s unhappiness with the set-up exploded during his night out in The Rex Rooms – with the consequences we have now.

It isn’t so much that England haven’t won a series for 20 months, and have just lost their first home series of three Tests or more for the first time in 14 years, though those facts are bad enough.

Joe Root must lead England to victory over Pakistan in this series. Defeat does not bear thinking about

But with Root and Marcus Trescothick (above) in charge it all feels like a blast from the past

It’s that the absence of any meaningful forward planning has left them with a captain whose lack of strategic acumen – obvious during his first 64 Tests in charge – was again evident during the 65th, against New Zealand at the Oval in June.

And with an interim coach who was part of McCullum’s uncritical inner coterie, and whose most notable contribution to the Ashes debacle was to suggest after the defeat in the second Test at Brisbane that England hadn’t discussed their loose dismissals during the first at Perth.

It’s a good job Pakistan find themselves at an even lower ebb, and possibly the lowest in their otherwise proud history, despite squaring their recent series in the Caribbean with a morale-boosting eight-wicket win over West Indies in Trinidad.

But that followed a 2–0 defeat in Bangladesh, and was one of only seven wins in their last 26 Tests stretching back to the middle of 2022, a sequence that also includes 17 defeats. They have not won a series in England since 1996.

The only team they have beaten in the last three years? That will be England in October 2024, when they employed giant fans and heaters to turn the pitches at Multan and Rawalpindi into dustbowls, a move that was mysteriously waved through by the ICC.

Their task this time has been made harder by the news that Babar Azam, their returning captain and star batsman, will miss the first Test after taking a blow on the right hand from Hampshire’s young fast bowler Manny Lumsden during last week’s warm-up game in Beckenham.

Babar is expected to be fit for the second Test at Lord’s, but his absence here – at a time when he was threatening to return to form after a barren run – has deprived the tourists of one of the world-class players in their ranks capable of making England’s life difficult. Salman Agha, who has led Pakistan in 50 T20s and a single one-day international, will take over, adding to the sense of two teams making it up as they go along.

In Babar’s absence, the player most likely to cause England problems is Mohammad Abbas, a probing seamer whose 897 first-class wickets have cost 20 each, and whose long CV includes stints at four counties. Armed with the familiar Dukes ball at a damp Headingley – and the forecast is mixed – he ought to be a handful.

Up against him is an England top order that confirm the make-do-and-mend nature of their Test team. Emilio Gay tailed off during his debut series against New Zealand after a promising start, and warmed up for this game with a pair for the Professional County Club Select XI against the Pakistanis.

Pakistan will be without their skipper Babar Azam (left) for the first Test but will have the canny bowling of Mohammad Abbas to call upon

Jordan Cox will bat at No 3 only two games after making his debut at No 7 as England indulge in yet more whack-a-mole

Jordan Cox, meanwhile, will bat at No 3, only two games after making his debut at No 7. England’s relentless game of whack-a-mole, dealing with one crisis before another pops up, shows no sign of stopping any time soon.

Neither has it helped that Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue, two members of their first-choice seam attack, were involved in the final of the Hundred on Sunday evening at Lord’s. There, they hurled themselves into the fray for Manchester Super Giants, a franchise 70 per cent owned by a Kolkata-based business conglomerate whose main interest is not the fortunes of England’s Test team but a sizeable return on their £81million investment.

If anything exposed the lunatic nature of the schedule, and the priorities of the ECB, it is the idea that these two crucial bowlers will automatically be able to switch codes.

It is not just the Test team who are flying by the seat of their pants: it is the whole of English cricket, squeezing in fixtures and formats, and hoping no one collapses in a heap. That may be good enough to see off Pakistan over the next few weeks, but England fans will need some convincing that it’s a recipe for regaining the Ashes.

Sports.title: Sky Sports DROP Baller League after 'partnership came to natural end' - with celebrity-backed competition 'keen to become free-to-air'
Sports.content:
Sports broadcasting giants Sky Sports have ended their coverage of Baller League from next season after opting not to renew their contract.

The competition, which has since its inception been backed by the likes of KSI, Gary Lineker and Ian Wright, sold out the O2 Arena for last season's final, which was won by KSI's Prime FC.

According to The Guardian, Sky are said to have been happy with viewing figures and social media interaction, but feel the partnership has come to a natural end.

The first UK edition of the tournament, which is an indoor six-a-side competition, took place in 2025 and follows a common trend of the growth in power of influencers.

The teams were usually made up of former professional footballers or those without a club, and have also been managed by the likes of Chloe Kelly and Angry Ginge.

It had first launched in Germany a year prior, inspired by Spain's Kings League, with backing from footballers Mats Hummels and Lukas Podolski.

Sky Sports had ended its partnership with Baller League, who are keen to make the competition free-to-air

Chief executive Felix Starck told The Guardian that the organisation had not tried to extend its deal with Sky and is keen to make its shows free-to-air. It is reported, though, that talks with Comcast, Sky's parent company, did take place.

They are said to now be focusing on expanding their YouTube profile.

The Baller League is made up of 12 teams and there are rolling subs throughout games.

Each team plays each other once in back-to-back matches on Monday nights, with the final four at the end of the season progressing to the semi-finals, before the final decides the winner of the league.

Sports.title: Jordan Cox reveals inspirational message from India legend Virat Kohli as England bosses tell him to 'go out there and have fun' in unfamiliar No 3 slot against Pakistan
Sports.content:
Jordan Cox reveals inspirational message from India legend Virat Kohli as England bosses tell him to 'go out there and have fun' in unfamiliar No 3 slot against Pakistan

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England’s new No 3 Jordan Cox has revealed how Indian legend Virat Kohli helped him deal with the disappointment of missing out on a Test debut two years ago because of injury.

The 25-year-old Cox, who has been told to ‘go out there and have fun’ in Wednesday’s first Test against Pakistan at Headingley, feared he might never get another chance at the highest level after breaking his thumb shortly before the first Test against New Zealand at Christchurch in November 2024.

‘It felt like that was the end, as bad as that sounds,’ Cox told the BBC. ‘I remember talking to Virat about it. He said: “There are billions of people who don’t even know who I am. The sun will come up in the morning.”

Cox, who has been part of Kohli’s Royal Challengers Bengaluru squad in the IPL, said he spoke again to the former India captain before his debut against New Zealand at The Oval in June, when he made 27 and 25 from No 7.

‘He was just saying: “Enjoy the moment. You only get one debut. Just enjoy it and have fun,”’ said Cox. ‘He’s someone I’ve looked up to and I’ve managed to spend what felt like four months in India. He’s someone I’ll text if I’m ever feeling down or need a bit of help. He’s always at the end of the phone.’

Jordan Cox has never batted at No3 before but will take the key position against Pakistan

His selection for the first two Tests against Pakistan came about because of Jacob Bethell’s knee injury, lending a circular feel to recall - when Cox missed out in Christchurch, it was Bethell who made his debut at No 3 instead.

‘That’s professional sport, isn’t it?’ he said. ‘I missed out on my debut two years ago and Jacob’s done incredibly well. He now gets injured and hopefully I do incredibly well.’

News of his call-up was broken on the phone during the Hundred by Marcus North, the new national selector, who told him: ‘I’m going to give you clarity: you’re going to bat three for the two Test matches. Basically, go out there, have fun, do what you’ve been doing, don’t change the way you’ve been playing in county cricket.’

Cox, who has averaged 68 in first-class cricket for Essex since leaving his native Kent after the 2023 season, does have experience against the new ball, having opened 30 times for his first county. But he isn’t about to sweat the details.

‘If England ask you to bat one to 11, I would say “yes”. Seven was great fun, the ball was a bit older, and I got to bat with Joe Root, which was pretty cool.

'If England call you and go “You’re batting anywhere,” you go: “Absolutely, I’ll do my best to go and win a Test match.”’

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher reveals why Man United will NOT win the Premier League under Michael Carrick as Sky Sports pundit names the Spurs signing the Red Devils should have landed
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick lacks the 'stardust' to return Manchester United to the pinnacle of football, claims Jamie Carragher.

Carrick, 45, landed the Old Trafford gig on a permanent basis this summer having impressed during his interim stint in charge of the club following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January.

The former United midfielder led the Red Devils to victories over Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool to deliver a third-place finish, returning the club to the Champions League after two seasons out of the competition.

Carrick's strong start to life in the United dugout has led to a groundswell of optimism among fans that he can oversee the club's first league title since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure in 2013.

However, Liverpool legend Carragher has urged caution ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

'I'm not saying it's going to go wrong. What Manchester United have had for the last six months, need that for another 12 months of not being the circus, not being the story all the time, and Carrick brings you that,' he said on The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet.

Michael Carrick lacks the 'stardust' to deliver a Premier League or Champions League title for Manchester United, Jamie Carragher has claimed

Carrick has landed the United job on a permanent basis after an impressive interim spell

'But has he got that stardust to win the biggest trophy? And I think you need to get to a strong position of being a proper Champions League club again. And then, right, what do we need? It's like a player gets you to a certain level, then we need that stardust.

'I personally just don't think Michael Carrick's got that stardust as a manager to win a Champions League or a Premier League.

'I don't believe Michael Carrick will win the league or the Champions League with Manchester United, but he's done a really good job.

'He could have a good season and put Manchester United in a position to then go and get a Champions League-winning manager.'

Carrick has sought to strengthen his squad in the summer transfer market, with midfielders Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans arriving from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively.

But Carragher believes United missed a trick in not pursuing former West Ham star Mateus Fernandes, with the club baulking at his £85million asking price. The midfielder has since joined Spurs.

‘I was a little bit worried when I saw United linked with Fernandes because I thought that could be a good signing,’ he said.

‘I just looked at him and his age and was surprised United didn’t go for Fernandes. They said it was too expensive but was it that expensive?

Carragher believes Carrick can set a good foundation for the next Man United manager

He also questioned why the Red Devils pulled out of a move for £85m Mateus Fernandes

‘I know £85m is a lot but you’re never going to get a really top midfielder now for £50m.’

Elsewhere, United legend Paul Scholes believes the defence is 'still a problem', with United yet to bring in fresh additions at the back.

'Centre halves are still a problem,' he said. 'Manchester United still need better centre halves – the current players don't have the quality, where I am judging Manchester United, to go on and win the Premier League.

'You need centre halves who are reliable every single week. We've got Maguire who has started to pick up some [injury] niggles, Lisandro Martinez – the lad just can't stay fit now. When he's fit, he is a good player, don't get me wrong.

'They've got Leny Yoro who has struggled over the last two years – it looks like the [Premier League] level is above him and [hopefully] he might come on [a bit this season].'

Former Bayern Munich defender Matthijs de Ligt has been sidelined since November with a long-term back injury, with no clear sign as to when he will return.

Scholes believes the 27-year-old is the club's best defender – if he can stay fit.

'If de Ligt is fit and playing every week, he's possibly Manchester United's best centre-half. But again, that's a question mark against centre-halves. You can't have those question marks.'

Sports.title: 'I was a young wolf,' admits new boss Sebastien Pocognoli as he promises to bring passion, energy and clear thinking to the Scotland job
Sports.content:
In a previous life, Sebastien Pocognoli was a young firebrand who certainly knew how to light the blue touchpaper back home in Belgium.

Whilst playing for his hometown club Standard Liege, Pocognoli was determined to lap it up after a 6-2 thrashing of their bitter rivals Charleroi back in 2012.

In an incident which carried echoes of Graeme Souness in Turkey, Pocognoli planted a Liege flag in the centre spot after the match and would later be charged and fined by police for inciting violence.

'It was a long time ago,' reflected the 39-year-old, who was unveiled as Scotland's new head coach after signing a two-year deal to replace Steve Clarke.

'I was a young wolf. But actually, it was slightly too much. I will not do that again. Be careful with passion. Too much passion can be also too much and cross the line.

'You need to find the balance - to be analytic and to be passionate. If you just react only with passion, you make mistakes.

Scotland's new head coach, Sebastien Pocognoli, gets a feel for the pitch at Hampden Park

'I am passionate but I also try to be analytical. I am very energetic on the touchline and in my relationship with the players.

'But I also try to be calm in the right moments because I need to make good choices and I need to have a clear head.

'You also need a good staff around you to help to have a good voice and give good advice. Yes, passion is good but you cannot react to everything with fire.'

If Pocognoli can bring success to Scotland and bring a more modern style of play, the Tartan Army will get fully on board with the new Wolf of Mount Florida.

He was calm and measured at Hampden today, speaking alongside SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell and chief football officer Craig Mulholland, both of whom led the recruitment process.

Pocognoli spoke decent English and expressed his desire to play on the front foot whilst bringing through young players and refreshing the squad.

All of this would have been music to the ears of most Scotland fans. The whole setup had gone flat and stale under Clarke, underlined by Scotland's miserable offering in the World Cup.

Maxwell also spoke today about the need for the country to embrace change, to embrace a more modern approach, and the feeling that Scotland are ready for a new direction.

That is, of course, broadly correct. But there was a slight irony in the fact that the change has almost happened by accident, with Clarke walking away from a four-year deal handed to him prior to the World Cup.

Had that resignation not happened, we wouldn't be in this position. But that's by the by. Pocognoli is the man entrusted with taking Scotland forward and bringing a sense of excitement and ambition to the team.

In terms of his credentials, he had a short stint in charge of Monaco last season. He won 16 of his 38 matches, scored plenty of goals, albeit they conceded quite a few at the other end as well.

The highlight was a 3-1 win away from home over Paris Saint-Germain, part of a home and away double over the European champions. Pocognoli also oversaw victories over Marseille and Lyon.

At USG in Belgium, he won a championship, which was the club's first league title in 90 years. With the SFA tapping into data now more than ever before, he ticked a lot of boxes.

If it's a risky appointment or a gamble, the SFA have rolled the dice and done exactly what many fans have been asking them to do.

'Like many coaches, you say you want to be dominant,' said Pocognoli of his style of play. 'That's the reality.

'But, of course, it is easy to say be dominant on paper and in training tell that to the players, but to make it happen in the heads of the players in games is a big difference.

'I like to defend on the front foot, be high up the pitch. The risk is to give some space at the back but there is more chance to be dangerous high up the pitch.

Pocognoli was appointed after a recruitment process led by Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell

'So yes, to be direct, have good passing options and keep the qualities of Scottish football - be passionate, win more duels than the opponent. That to me is very important.

'Change can be a really aggressive word. It's not like changing the page in a book. It is about trying to continue and trying to improve for the benefit of Scottish football.

'I hope I can be the right man for this two-year contract and I think Craig and Ian really want to help the process to continue to develop Scottish football in terms of structure.

'Also, following the young talent, to work more closely with the clubs and to try to improve things. It's a positive approach and I hope it will be a good fit.'

One of the main criticisms levelled at Clarke over the years was his reluctance to give a chance to young players, that he became too loyal and too reliant on the old guard.

The likes of Findlay Curtis, Lennon Miller and Kieron Bowie now have a manager who seems far more open to blooding young talent.

Indeed, a key part of the remit for Pocognoli is helping bring through the next generation, whilst still delivering results in the here and now.

Robbie Ure is another who should be firmly on his radar, the young striker having just completed a big-money move to Sevilla.

'That is in my baggage - to work with young players,' said the new Scotland boss, whose first matches will come against Slovenia and Switzerland when the Nations League gets under way next month.

'It is easier to do in daily work, because you can help them daily. At the end of my playing career I went straight into an academy at Union SG and Genk and also the national team when you are 18-20 years old.

'I know the routine of the national teams and how players have to get used to that routine.

'In Union it was a project to develop players. That is something I like to do. At Monaco in a short period of time I developed many good players.

'You can see they sold a lot of players this summer and I was only there for six months. That shows what I can do.

'But the national team needs a different approach, you need the clubs, you need to have the support from clubs and I hope I can stimulate this.

'It's to find the right balance between trying to get the right results, otherwise you will be on me! And also to find the opportunity to develop some players.

Pocognoli says it is 'really positive' to see young Scots such as Kieron Bowie playing in Italy

'When you test or try things, it's also a part of risk. You have to accept that I'll try to get the benefit of a result and also develop and be ready for what is coming next season. I want to go through the processes and challenges.

'I think there are some exciting names who will come [into the squad]. It will depend who is progressing at their clubs and what they achieve.

'It is not easy to go at a very young age in Italy [as Miller and Bowie have done] with very specific football culture. But it can only be really positive for Scottish football.

'There are a lot of names to follow. But also I would like to see these young names growing in the top clubs in Scotland because that's where you want to see them. That is something very important for me too, to follow the young talents here.'

The winds of change have blown through Hampden. There is a freshness to all of this. A lot of Scotland fans will be on board with Pocognoli purely because of the fact he's not Steve Clarke.

If the Belgian can deliver a modern, attacking brand of football and impart meaningful change, the Tartan Army could be set for an exciting new chapter.

Sports.title: York Ebor tips: Newsboy's race-by-race day one picks of festival
Sports.content:
The York Ebor Festival is often dubbed the Royal Ascot of the North.

But it is a fantastic meeting in its own right and a jewel in the crown of the Flat season.

The four-day extravaganza gets underway on Wednesday with a fantastic card and the Juddmonte International takes centre stage

The Daily Mirror’s Chief Tipster,Newsboy, aka David Yates, predicts his 1-2-3 in each race on day one.

‌



1.50 Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

1 THE MAN

2 LEXINGTON BLITZ

‌



3 AIR FORCE ONE

THE MAN , edged out by Trefor in this race 12 months ago, is weighted to go one better.

Having landed a course-and-distance handicap at the Dante fixture in May 2025, the Richard Spencer-trained son of Mehmas was absent through the summer before going off at 15-2 against 19 opponents.

And The Man so nearly took his record on the Knavesmire to two wins from three attempts, leading over a furlong from the finish but headed in the closing stages and going under by a head.

‌



Beaten at Southwell in September on his final outing of last season, my selection had his first three starts of this year in Dubai, following a sixth in a Group 2 contest in January by claiming the same finishing position in two handicaps.

The Man was messed about leaving the stalls when 11th in Newcastle’s Gosforth Park Cup after 112 days off but his run behind Twilight Calls at Glorious Goodwood - although 13th, he was just over three lengths behind the winner - was a bit more like it.

Connections persevere with the cheekpieces and tongue strap applied that day and The Man gets the vote to take advantage of a mark 3lb lower than for last August’s near-miss.

Lexington Blitz, Trefor and Air Force One are just three dangers in a trappy start to the fixture.

‌



2.25 Tattersalls Acomb Stakes

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

1 HAFFNER

2 GENTLE HURRICANE

‌



3 ALFRED WALLACE

HAFFNER rates a worthy favourite to register a second career success - and a first at Group level.

The son of Justify went off at 18-1 for his racecourse bow in a six-furlong maiden at the Curragh at the end of June - a race for which his Aidan O’Brien-saddled stablemate Abraham Lincoln started the 11-8 market leader.

The favourite did indeed oblige but Haffner ran with abundant promise to finish a length-and-three-quarter runner-up, particularly considering he showed signs of inexperience both before and during the race.

‌



Ryan Moore’s partner duly went one better on the final day of Newmarket’s July Festival, landing a seven-furlong maiden by a length and a half from Al Wathba - a performance that led to a challenge for the Group 2 Vintage Stakes over the same distance at Glorious Goodwood 22 days ago.

Sent off at 4-1 in a field of six, Haffner took another step forward with a second to Dr Rascal, battling on determinedly in the closing stages to be beaten half a length by an unbeaten, and smart, two-year-old.

My choice drops a notch down the class ladder to Group 3 company here and, with more to come, is poised to take full advantage.

Salisbury scorer Gentle Hurricane is feared most, ahead of Alfred Wallace and Stardom Glory.

‌



3.00 Great Voltigeur Stakes

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

1 PIERRE BONNARD

2 MALTESE CROSS

‌



3 CHRISTMAS DAY

View 2 Images Pierre Bonnard is Newsboy's selection in the Great Voltigeur (Image: PA)

PIERRE BONNARD is fancied to win for the first time in 2026 and book his place in the line-up for next month’s St Leger.

‌



It was little surprise to see Camelot’s son spend the winter as favourite for the Derby - Pierre Bonnard’s progress as a two-year-old saw him go from victory in a Dundalk maiden to success in the Group 3 Zetland Stakes at Newmarket and the Group 1 Critérium de Saint-Cloud.

His supporters’ dreams of Epsom glory suffered a jolt when Pierre Bonnard could manage just seventh place behind his Aidan O’Brien stable-companion Christmas Day in the Group 3 Ballysax Stakes at Leopardstown.

And my selection suffered another reverse, albeit via a short-head second to James J Braddock, when the 5-6 hotpot for the same-level Derby Trial Stakes in Foxrock four weeks later.

A gamble into 7-2 for the Derby itself went astray as Pierre Bonnard came home in seventh behind Christmas Day - subsequent Group 1 Grand Prix de Paris winner Maltese Cross ran second - but a 10-length deficit was reduced to a neck when the pair filled the podium behind Ballydoyle’s Benvenuto Cellini in the Irish version at the Curragh.

‌



The market principals must each shoulder a 5lb penalty so the door is open for Pierre Bonnard to turn the tables, with the improving Superior Choice another to consider.

3.35 Juddmonte International

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

1 ITEM

‌



2 OMBUDSMAN

3 CONSTITUTION RIVER

ITEM is well capable of playing the role of disruptor in a race billed as a clash between Ombudsman and Constitution River.

A two-year-old campaign that yielded victories in a maiden at Kempton Park and a novice stakes at Bath in September - heavy ground saw Item scratched from the Group 1 Futurity Trophy at Doncaster the following month - promised much for the Andrew Balding trainee’s Classic season.

‌



It seemed only right that Balding gave Frankel’s son his comeback in the Group 2 Dante Stakes over this afternoon’s course and distance.

And connections had little choice but to roll the Derby dice when Colin Keane’s mount galloped to a two-and-three-quarter-length winning margin from Action.

When it came to the big day, the weather gods refused to play ball - torrential rain turned the going to ‘soft’ - and Item’s chances sank in the Epsom mud with a ninth-of-14 finish behind Dante third Christmas Day.

But the return to quicker terrain for the Group 2 York Stakes, again over today’s course and distance, saw Item rediscover his mojo.

‌



Carrying a 3lb penalty as a result of his Dante win, the three-year-old humbled his four senior rivals, strong at the finish to hold Pride Of Arras by two and three-quarter lengths.

The way the closing stages unfolded - Item was caught flat-footed before asserting - suggests a stern gallop set by defending champion Ombudsman’s pacemaker Devil’s Advocate will help Item on his return to the highest level.

Another personal best will doubtless be required - Ombudsman and Constitution River have won six Group 1 prizes between them - but it will be a surprise if my selection doesn’t have a good deal more to give.

4.10 Sky Bet Stayers’ Handicap

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

1 TEAM PLAYER

2 SMALL FRY

3 SHRIMP SHADY

‌



TEAM PLAYER is expected to give another good account of himself.

A two-time winner in the care of Gemma Tutty, the gelded son of Without Parole joined Ewan Whillans during the winter and began his time with the Hawick-based trainer with a victory in a two-mile handicap at Newcastle in February.

Whillans then took aim at the valuable Queen’s Cup at Musselburgh in April and Team Player netted the £25,770 first prize with a length-and-three-quarter beating of Dancingwithmyself.

The winning run came to an end in the Chester Cup but Greg Fairley’s partner came home with gusto to finish fifth to A Piece Of Heaven, and a funeral cortège worked against Team Player, fitted with cheekpieces and a tongue strap, when he finished ninth of 20 behind Align The Stars in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle.

‌



But the four-year-old showed his true colours at Newbury last time out, going under by a nose to Shrimp Shady, and a 2lb nudge up the weights should not be enough to stop this likeable stayer from showing to the fore here.

Shrimp Shady, second at the Shergar Cup 11 days ago, should be on the scene once again, in company with Newbury third Ride The Thunder and favourite Small Fry.

4.45 Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

‌



1 UNDERWRITER

2 NAANA’S SHADOW

3 POATAN

UNDERWRITER deserves the chance to prove his last-time-out Ascot fourth was no flash in the pan.

‌



A £200,000 breeze-up purchase in the spring of last year, Underwriter went into training with Archie Watson and carried the Wathnan Racing livery to success in a maiden and novice stakes at Ayr.

The son of Mehmas then lost his way and, when a gelding operation failed to trigger an upturn in his fortunes this season, Underwriter joined Michael Keady for 4,600 guineas in June.

His stable debut yielded an 11th-of-12 finish behind Twilight Calls at Newmarket’s July Festival.

But those who backed the three-year-old each-way at 100-1 for the five-furlong handicap that wrapped up the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes undercard were unlucky not to collect on place part as Underwriter returned fourth of 13 to All Ways Glamorous.

‌



He would have made the podium with a clear run and Luke Morris’s mount is expected to go well from an unchanged British Horseracing Authority rating of 84.

Naana’s Shadow continues to go from strength to strength and heads the list of dangers, with Manatee Mehmas and Poatan others to merit a second glance.

5.20 Sky Bet Nursery Handicap

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3

‌



1 HAVANA SPRITE

2 HENLEY ON THAMES

3 SOVEREIGN GLORY

HAVANA SPRITE is on a roll - and isn’t done with yet.

‌



On the back of in-the-frame efforts at Newmarket and Great Yarmouth in May, the James Tate-trained daughter of Havana Grey made it third time lucky by beating four opponents for a fillies’ novice stakes at Bath the following month.

Twelve days later, Havana Sprite shared the spoils with Glorious Game when the pair dead-heated for the Listed Empress Fillies’ Stakes at Newmarket.

But she was allowed to keep the prize outright when entering handicap company back at the July Course on her most recent outing, leading at the furlong pole to hold Acclamation Star by half a length.

The handicapper couldn’t get too carried away with that form and Havana Sprite competes from a British Horseracing Authority rating of 92 after a 4lb intervention.

‌



But Hector Crouch’s partner keeps coming up with personal bests and, with the upward curve unlikely to flatten out just yet, she is the selection to go in again.

In a field of lightly raced juveniles, Henley On Thames, Ruler’s Pride and Sovereign Glory are just three horses who can get involved.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney reveals he's had NOSE surgery as Man Utd icon admits 'it's uncomfortable'
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney reveals he's had NOSE surgery as Man Utd icon admits 'it's uncomfortable'

Wayne Rooney has gone a big transformation since his playing days with Manchester United and the Red Devils icon has now revealed that he has gone under the knife over recent days

View 2 Images

Manchester United icon Wayne Rooney has revealed he has finally had surgery to fix a broken nose EIGHT YEARS late. The Red Devils hero suffered the issue when playing for MLS side DC United back in 2018 but decided to delay corrective surgery.

‌



The 40-year-old continued his playing career with Derby County, before turning to management with the Rams, while he also had stints with DC United, Birmingham City and Plymouth Argyle.

‌



Having now moved into the media, Rooney has revealed that he has now undergone surgery to fix his nose. Speaking on the first episode of Stick to United, Rooney said: “I had surgery on my nose last week.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I’m actually really lucky I’ve got no black eyes. But I’ve still got two plastic tubes up my nose which are coming out very soon. I can’t wait for them to come out. They’ve cut here so that’s all stitched. It’s a little bit uncomfortable.”

He added: “I broke my nose against Preston in the FA Cup. It was when all that Wade Barrett stuff came out because it was a bit of a dive. I won a penalty. I broke my nose in that game and then, when I went to DC United, I broke my nose again. That was a bad one.

‌



“I needed surgery but I never had it. I put it off. This summer I thought I’d get the World Cup out of the way and I’ll get it done. I had it done last week. It went well but these tubes are horrible and they’re still in.”

View 2 Images Rooney broke his nose during his time in MLS (Image: Getty Images)

Rooney’s comments come after he was asked about his former club’s summer transfer business so far, the former forward claiming that four positions still need strengthening before the deadline.

‌



Rooney said: “I thought Luke Shaw had a really good season last season, but he didn’t have the best game against AC Milan. So I don’t think you can rely on Luke Shaw to be consistent for the whole season.

“That leads me to Lewis-Skelly, and we’re hearing that he’s available for not much money. I think it’s an absolute no-brainer.

“If you can get a player who can play left-back, he can play centre midfield. He’s young, he’s got a massive future ahead of him. I think it’s an absolute no-brainer if you can bring him in.

Article continues below

“I’d like to see another centre-back, I’d like to see another central midfield player and another centre forward.

“So I think there’s still a lot of work there to be done, but I think it’s really important that the players they do bring in, they get it right and they get the right players in.”

Sports.title: Man Utd forced into kit change before season has started to avoid rule break
Sports.content:
Man Utd forced into kit change before season has started to avoid rule break

Manchester United have had to make a change to one of their new kits already this summer

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes in the new Manchester United third kit (Image: 2026 Eurasia Sport Images)

Manchester United have been forced to make a change to one of their kits before the season has even kicked off in order to avoid breaking UEFA rules. The club’s new third strip was released last week.

‌



It features three eye-catching central logos: the Red Devil crest, a Snapdragon fireball emblem and an Adidas' three-stripe logo. It marks a rapid departure from the club's home and away kits this season, as it doesn't feature 'Snapdragon' written across the front of the shirt.

‌



The Old Trafford outfit have explained that they will have to alter the shirt for the Champions League, however. This means United's third shirt in Europe will feature the Snapdragon word mark, the same as their home and away strip, and not the Snapdragon symbol.

‌



UEFA insist that jerseys worn in the Champions League must all be consistent with one another, meaning United's third kit must stay consistent their home and away.

A club statement read: "You have probably noticed that there is a different look to the latter, too. Our new third shirt doesn't feature the traditional 'Snapdragon' wordmark, yet the sponsor is still recognisable through its fireball, which has been ever-present on United's jerseys since the start of the 2024/25 campaign.

Man Utd holding Bruno Fernandes future talks after big money offer received READ MORE :

"On our latest release, it forms part of an aesthetic three-pronged design down the centre of the shirt, done in agreement with adidas and Snapdragon to provide the jersey with a fresh style and clean look that is unique for this season.

‌



"The Reds are due to sport the jersey when required across domestic competition this term, although UEFA rules mean that the 'Snapdragon' wordmark will be added to our players' shirts for any Champions League matches it is worn in.

"This is because the same version of a logo must be used across all of a club's kits in the tournament, so the sponsor on the third strip needs to match that on our new home and away releases, which feature the wordmark."

View 3 Images United's third shirt will have to align with the club's home shirt in the Champions League (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



Snapdragon have been the club's primary sponsor since the beginning of the 2024/25 season. Sportswear giant Adidas signed a 10-year deal with United in 2023 worth a staggering £900million.

Michael Carrick‘s side will kick off their Premier League season with an away trip to newly-promoted Hull on Saturday. They end the summer having suffered two defeats in pre-season against Wrexham and Milan, but they secured wins against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid, and drew against Paris Saint-Germain and Leeds.

"I think, as a whole, it's been good," Carrick told MUTV. "I think there are a lot of positives to take from it. I think a lot of the performances, I think the group has grown and got stronger.

‌



View 3 Images United's third kit will look slightly different in the Champions League (Image: © 2026 SOPA Images)

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"But on the whole, we're ready for next week. I think a lot of the boys will be better for the minutes, and as I said, we've done a lot of work on the training pitch. I think the performances in the games have been pretty good, so we're still in good spirits going into next week."

‌



United are also back amongst Europe’s elite for the first time in three years. They will find out their Champions League fate when the fixture list for the league phase is drawn on August 26.

The club will be in pot two. United will play eight league games, four at home and four away, but will not face another Premier League side.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd coach warns Michael Carrick his Old Trafford honeymoon could be over
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd coach warns Michael Carrick his Old Trafford honeymoon could be over

Former Man Utd coach Rene Meulensteen fears European football could prove a huge problem for Michael Carrick at Old Trafford this coming season

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has to face the demands of Champions League football this season

Michael Carrick has been told his honeymoon period as Manchester United boss could be over.

‌



Carrick worked wonders in the second half of last season after replacing the sacked Ruben Amorim on a caretaker basis. He engineered some seismic wins, to lead United to Champions League qualification.

‌



But Carrick has been warned that this achievement could come back to bite him this time round. Former United coach Rene Meulensteen reckons managing the increased workload of European football could lead to Carrick and his side's downfall.

‌



Meulensteen, who was No.1 to Sir Alex Ferguson at Old Trafford, said: "The number of games they're going to be playing is something completely different to last season.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Michael is going to have to manage the squad extremely well, because last season they played once a week and had plenty of time for recovery and probably more days off as well.

‌



"Whereas this season will be completely different as the volume of games, training sessions, and recovery days will change drastically. Not only that, but the travel time between games, especially playing in Europe, will have a huge impact as well.

"That's going to be something that United and Carrick have to come to terms with very quickly in the early stages of the season. Are they strong enough to handle it? If the squad stays the way it is currently, I doubt it."

View 2 Images Rene Meulensteen worked alongside Sir Alex Ferguson at Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Meulensteen also believes United's defensive consistency will be crucial if they are to cope with the demands of the season. He added: "I still think they're vulnerable at the back - and that's one thing Michael is going to have to sort out as soon as possible when the season starts.

"Finding a centre-back partnership that works, and getting some consistency in the back line will be key. Harry Maguire is coming off a good end to last season, but he needs some complimentary centre backs next to him.

"They have plenty of options at centre back in (Lisandro) Martinez, (Leny) Yoro, (Ayden) Heaven and even Luke Shaw can play in the position.

‌



"But the problem has been that inconsistency at the back, which he will need to sort out as soon as possible.”

Sports.title: Four players Arsenal could sell before window closes after Mikel Arteta complaints
Sports.content:
Four players Arsenal could sell before window closes after Mikel Arteta complaints

Arsenal are running out of time to sell unwanted players in the summer transfer window and Mikel Arteta voiced his frustrations following their Community Shield win on Sunday

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal have too many players for a matchday squad (Image: Ryan Pierse/The FA via Getty Images)

Arsenal are looking to offload four fringe players who failed to make the squad for their Community Shield win over Manchester City on Sunday. The Gunners kicked off their campaign by thrashing their Premier League title rivals 3-0, with Mikel Arteta's squad giving a hint at potential transfer exits.

‌



While all eyes were on new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis, who made their competitive debuts in Cardiff, Arteta's squad said plenty about those not included. Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Ethan Nwaneri, Marli Salmon, Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson were all missing from the matchday squad.

‌



Martinelli is the subject of interest from Galatasaray who have tabled a bid worth €45million (£38m) for the striker, who is reportedly not keen on moving to Turkey. The Brazilian forward has entered the final year of his contract, but appears likely to stay put unless a different transfer proposal emerges.

‌



Salmon is a 16-year-old defender who has made four first-team appearances for Arsenal, but will have to remain patient for further opportunities. The other four players who were uninvolved at the weekend could be sold before the September 1 transfer deadline.

‌



The Athletic reports that Vieira and Nelson are the subject of interest from Hamburg and West Ham respectively after spending last season away on loan. Meanwhile, Napoli are keen to sign Jesus, who is in the final 12 months of his deal, and the Gunners could reluctantly part company with Nwaneri too.

Nwaneri faces a challenge to get minutes in Arsenal's stacked midfield and there is a grudging realisation that a transfer may be the best outcome, especially as the homegrown player would count as pure profit on the balance sheet. The 19-year-old spent last season on loan with Marseille and AC Milan and Galatasaray are among the clubs to formally make enquiries this summer.

The competition for places at Arsenal has led to the club needing to offload fringe players, with Arteta frustrated that he can't include more players on the substitutes' bench.

‌



View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri was in Cardiff on Sunday but didn't make the squad (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

“It’s really sad not to have their availability," Arteta told TNT Sports after the win. "I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend and accommodate more players in the squad because they deserve to be in the squad, there’s no question.

“Ethan and Marli as well, who has had the whole pre-season with us. Hopefully we can change that rule so players can enjoy on the pitch and can be an option to play and contribute to the team going forward.”

‌



Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta is working hard to try and agree some sales, with Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) the only players have left the club for transfer fees this summer.

Sales are needed to help fund incoming deals for a central defender to provide cover for the injured William Saliba and world-class attacker.

Sports.title: Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiance Wladimir Klitschko breaks silence after tragic death
Sports.content:
Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiance Wladimir Klitschko breaks silence after tragic death

US actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, died aged 36 and had previously been engaged to former heavyweight boxer Wladimir Klitschko

Hollywood actress Hayden Panettiere from Heroes and Nashville dies age 36

Former heavyweight boxing world champion Wladimir Klitschko has expressed his "shock and grief" following the death of his ex-fiancee Hayden Panettiere.

‌



US actress Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, died aged 36 on Sunday afternoon. Panettiere was found in her home by police in Greenville, South Carolina. Officers responded to a call made by an acquaintance reporting that the actress was “unresponsive” and in “cardiac arrest”.

‌



There were “no signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances” relating to Panettiere's death. She and Klitschko were together for 10 years and had a daughter together in 2014. And the former boxer took to social media to say: "Our family is going through a time of profound shock and grief.

‌



View 3 Images Hayden Panettiere with Wladimir Klitschko in 2011 (Image: Lev Radin/Shutterstock)

"The announcement of Hayden’s tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya. She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry. Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives.

"To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was. I extend my deepest condolences to Hayden’s parents, her friends, and her fans, who are also grieving today. Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon.

‌



"I ask everyone to please respect our family’s feelings and privacy during this incredibly difficult time. For now, this is all I wish to say. Thank you to everyone who is supporting my family and expressing their sincere condolences. Rest easy, Hayden. May you find eternal peace."

Panettiere and Klitschko began dating in 2009 at a party before splitting briefly two years later. They soon reconciled and Panettiere was photographed with a ring on her wedding finger, but the couple's engagement was not confirmed until 2013 before Panettiere announced she was pregnant the following year.

After a traumatic birth, Panettiere suffered from post-natal depression and eventually checked into rehab, giving full custody of daughter Kaya to Klitschko.

‌



Panettiere began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas before gaining wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember The Titans alongside Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in Pixar’s 1998 film A Bug’s Life. Panettiere later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before going on to star as up-and-coming country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on the hit TV series Nashville.

3 View 3 Images Wladimir Klitschko with Hayden Panettiere (Image: Dave Allocca/Starpix/Shutterstock) 3 View 3 Images Wladimir Klitschko with Hayden Panettiere (Image: Action Press/Shutterstock)

‌



Her performances in Nashville earned her two Golden Globe nominations for best supporting actress while her singing on the show produced 11 entries on the US Billboard Hot Country Songs charts. Panettiere’s film credits include 2006’s Bring It On: All Or Nothing, comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed.

Following her rapid rise to fame, the pressure of the industry began to weigh on Panettiere – with the actress previously revealing that she had struggled with addiction throughout her 20s. In a memoir published earlier this year, Panettiere opened up about her struggles with mental health, the loss of her younger brother, Jansen, and her decision to give full custody of her daughter.

“The idea that anyone would think that I would just give away my child and be okay with it is heartbreaking and couldn’t be further from the truth,” she told podcaster Jay Shetty after the release of her memoir in May. Panettiere said her daughter had lived with her father full-time from a young age amid the actress’s struggles with addiction and mental health.

Article continues below

She said: “I was struggling with mental health and anxiety, and the postpartum and having to act my way through it and just feeling like I completely lost myself.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
