World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and whom Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the reintroduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. World.title: Prague’s Groovy Market Fest Returns After a Successful Debut
World.content:
A new urban festival is aiming to become a regular fixture on Prague’s cultural calendar after attracting 1,200 visitors to its first edition in Riegrovy sady.

Groovy Market Fest, held on August 1, brought together food, design, music and local brands in a format inspired by European city markets.

According to the organizers, around 85% of visitors were tourists or foreign residents of Prague, highlighting the event’s appeal beyond the Czech-speaking audience.



The festival will return to Riegrovy sady on September 5, with further editions planned for October, November and December.

From Barcelona to Prague

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food culture.

Their interest in international gastronomy also led them to compete in Spain. In 2025, they won first place in the Cooking The Street competition, where their dish was judged by a professional panel that included chefs Beñat Ormaetxea and Jon Kepa Aurrecoetxea.

After returning to Prague, they decided to develop their own event, drawing inspiration from markets such as Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market.

The First Edition

Food Garden focused on gastronomy, while Palm Street featured local products and handmade goods. The Design Zone presented Czech brands working in fashion, design and art.

Rather than filling the site with as many vendors as possible, the organizers selected a smaller number of participants. They say the approach was intended to create a more coherent experience for visitors.

Music was another part of the programme, with live performances and DJ sets throughout the event. Visitors could also attend a masterclass focused on preparing the festival’s signature Groovy cocktail.

Additional editions are scheduled for October 3, November 7 and December 5, all at the same location.

Tickets for upcoming editions are available through GoOut.

World.title: Faster Than the Metro. New Bus is Now Linking Prague 8 and Prague 6
World.content:
A new bus service running through Prague’s Blanka tunnel has begun operating, offering a direct connection between the northern part of the city and Dejvice.

Bus line 145 connects Čimice and Kobylisy in Prague 8 with Hradčanská and Dejvická in Prague 6. The journey takes around 15 minutes, according to Prague’s public transport authority ROPID.



The same trip by metro requires a change between lines C and A in the city centre and takes around 22 minutes.

Including the time spent walking through stations and using escalators, the journey can take about half an hour.

The first day of operation brought mostly positive results, with many buses arriving on time or even ahead of schedule. The real test will come during regular weekday traffic, when congestion around Prague is heavier.

Where the new bus runs

In the direction from Čimice to Dejvice, line 145 serves:

Sídliště Čimice – Čimice – Libeňská – Řepínská – Podhajská pole – Čimický háj – Písečná – Služská – Kobylisy – Okrouhlická – Vychovatelna – Hradčanská – Vítězné náměstí – Dejvická

The return route follows the same corridor in the opposite direction.

The key feature of line 145 is its use of the Blanka tunnel, allowing buses to avoid the city centre and provide a direct connection between Prague 8 and Prague 6.

The new route is expected to make commuting easier for residents of Čimice, Kobylisy and surrounding neighbourhoods, while providing an alternative to the metro for journeys towards Dejvice and Hradčanská.

World.title: Leo Express to Launch Direct Prague–Brno Trains in December
World.content:
Leo Express is set to begin operating direct trains between Prague and Brno in December, marking the private carrier’s first direct connection between the two cities.

The company has already been serving passengers in the South Moravian Region, but its trains have so far bypassed Brno.

Over the past year, travellers from towns such as Hodonín and Břeclav have been able to use Leo Express services to reach Prague, travelling via Přerov and Olomouc.



The new Prague–Brno service will change that, putting the carrier directly on one of the Czech Republic’s busiest rail routes.

There is, however, one limitation for passengers travelling to Prague.

Leo Express trains do not serve Prague Main Station. In Prague, passengers must use Praha-Libeň station, which may be less convenient for those travelling to the city centre.

Leo Express was founded by businessman Leoš Novotný and has operated passenger trains in the Czech Republic since 2012.

The company has gradually expanded its network in the Czech Republic and abroad, competing with established operators such as České dráhy and RegioJet.

The Prague–Brno connection is expected to become another important part of the company’s Czech network from December.

World.title: Romanian Community to Celebrate Culture and Traditions in Prague
World.content:
The Romanian community in Czechia will come together in Prague on September 6 for the 12th edition of the Romanian Celebration, an annual event highlighting Romanian culture, traditions and the community’s ties with Czech society.

The main event will take place at the Ethnographic Section of the National Museum of the Czech Republic in Kinský Park, Prague 5.

The program will bring together Romanian music, dance, food, literature and activities for children.



Organized by the Association of Romanians in the Czech Republic (ARRC), the event is part of a wider cultural project running from March 1 to November 30, 2026.

Visitors can expect traditional music and dance performances, educational activities for children, cultural exhibitions, book presentations and Romanian gastronomy.

The event is aimed at members of the Romanian community, Romanian-speaking families, children and young people, as well as Czech residents interested in Romanian culture.

According to ARRC, the project aims to preserve and promote Romanian cultural and linguistic identity among Romanians living in the Czech Republic while creating opportunities for greater interaction between the Romanian and Czech communities.

“Through this project, we aim to offer the Romanian community, Romanian speakers, and lovers of the Romanian language a space for meeting, dialogue, and celebration of our cultural values, while also contributing to the consolidation of intercultural relations between Romania and the Czech Republic,” the ARRC leadership said.

World.title: Czech Fish Farmers Take Emergency Measures Amid Prolonged Drought
World.content:
Fish farmers reduce or suspend supplementary feeding to lower oxygen consumption, reports say.

Fish farmers in the Czech Republic have begun taking emergency measures as a prolonged drought, worsened by high temperatures across Europe, strains water supplies.

Facing water shortages, fish farmers have reduced or suspended supplementary feeding to lower fish oxygen consumption, while ponds are being regularly aerated, according to the report.



Several ponds have also been netted earlier than usual.

In the Třeboň area, which delivers tons of carp for the Czech Christmas table, part of the 200-hectare Koclířov pond has been drained and the fish moved to holding tanks.

More than a third of the water is missing from the region’s famous system of fish ponds due to the drought. The water level in Lake Svět, for example, has fallen by 98 centimetres. High temperatures are also causing water to evaporate more quickly.

The Czech government is expected to address the 2027 budget, upcoming elections and measures to tackle worsening drought.

Prime Minister Andrej Babiš has pledged an extra CZK 4 billion for drought-related measures. If approved, ministers will present plans for implementing them.

World.title: Burgermeister to Open First Prague Restaurant on Wenceslas Square in 2027
World.content:
Berlin burger chain Burgermeister is preparing to enter the Czech market, with its first Prague restaurant expected to open in early 2027.

The company has chosen Wenceslas Square for its debut. The location will also serve as a base for Burgermeister’s planned expansion across the Czech Republic, with more restaurants already in the pipeline.

Burgermeister has built its reputation in Berlin over the past two decades, growing from a single restaurant in a former public toilet into an international chain with 32 locations across Germany and other European markets.



Burgermeister has not yet revealed the exact address or confirmed a specific opening date.

The Prague restaurant will follow the concept that made Burgermeister popular in Berlin. The chain focuses on freshly prepared burgers and fries, with part of its food production handled in-house. Its operations also include its own bakery.

From a former public toilet to an international burger chain

Burgermeister opened its first restaurant in the Kreuzberg district of Berlin in 2006. The location was far from a conventional restaurant site. It occupied a former public toilet beneath the railway tracks near Schlesisches Tor station.

The unusual setting quickly became part of the brand’s identity. Over the years, Burgermeister expanded beyond its original Berlin location and developed into a larger restaurant chain.

Today, the company has 32 branches and is pursuing its goal of building a pan-European network.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



You can get your ticket here.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: How Much Can a Prague Taxi Driver Really Earn Each Month
World.content:
For passengers, a taxi ride can make the job look straightforward. Pick someone up, drive them across Prague, wait for the next booking and repeat.

But the income of a full-time taxi driver depends on far more than the fare shown on the meter or app.

Drivers working through platforms such as Uber and Bolt can generate more than CZK 60,000 in gross monthly revenue when working around 40 to 50 hours a week. What they actually keep, however, is considerably less.



Gross income can exceed CZK 60,000

Official figures for Prague’s taxi sector put the average gross monthly pay at roughly CZK 38,000. Drivers who work full time through ride-hailing platforms can earn more, particularly when they concentrate on periods of high demand.

According to Ondřej Krátký, founder of the Czech taxi platform Liftago, drivers can typically earn about CZK 250 to CZK 350 per hour. At the lower end of the market, however, some drivers make only around CZK 80 an hour, which is difficult to turn into a sustainable income in Prague.

Official statistics may also underestimate the money generated by some drivers because not every journey is paid through an app. Cash payments remain part of the business.

Fuel and commissions take a large share

Most Prague taxi drivers operate as self-employed contractors and use their own cars. That means they are responsible for almost all of the costs associated with the job.

Fuel is one of the largest expenses. Someone driving every day can spend more than CZK 10,000 a month on petrol or diesel alone.

Ride-hailing platforms also take a percentage of each fare. Depending on the service and other conditions, commissions can account for roughly 20 to 25 percent of the fare. Drivers must also cover vehicle maintenance, repairs, commercial insurance and the mandatory social and health insurance payments required of self-employed workers.

Once these expenses are taken into account, the amount left from gross earnings can fall by a third or more.

For a full-time driver, a realistic monthly amount after operating costs can therefore be somewhere between CZK 22,000 and CZK 35,000. The exact figure depends on the car, fuel consumption, working hours, platform commissions and the number and type of trips completed.

Tips make only a small difference

Tips are unlikely to transform a taxi driver’s income in the Czech Republic.

Unlike in countries where tipping is a major part of service workers’ earnings, Czech passengers generally round up the fare or leave a relatively small amount.

Uber allows passengers to tip through its app for up to 30 days after a journey, with the full tip going to the driver. Bolt offers a similar feature.

For most drivers, however, tips remain a minor addition to their monthly income rather than a significant source of earnings.

Timing can make a bigger difference

Drivers can increase their income by choosing when and where they work.

Friday and Saturday nights are among the busiest periods in Prague, particularly in the city centre. When demand rises sharply, ride-hailing platforms can increase fares, allowing drivers to generate more revenue from the same number of working hours.

Major concerts, festivals and other large events can have a similar effect. Airport journeys can also be attractive because they tend to cover longer distances than short trips within the city.

World.title: Leaked: Fidesz could be dismantled within weeks as its fate rests with members – and János Lázár
World.content:
Fidesz’s leadership has tasked János Lázár with assessing the party’s internal condition, visiting its key organisations, holding consultations, providing direction and producing an internal assessment by September. Party members are also being asked for their views: not only are they being questioned about the reasons for the defeat, but also whether Fidesz should be dismantled and replaced by a new party or movement. There is even an opportunity to send a message to Viktor Orbán.

While the former prime minister is on holiday in the United States, Serbia and Croatia – or, according to some reports, holds discussions on a range of issues – Fidesz is pressing ahead with an internal assessment after suffering a historic defeat on April 12. According to rumours, the public face of the exercise is János Lázár, who once harboured ambitions of becoming prime minister and, alongside Orbán and former foreign minister Péter Szijjártó – now employed by BYD – was one of the faces of the losing 2026 campaign.

Former PM Orbán with Lázár and Szijjártó: the faces of the 2026 campaign. Photo: Facebook/Lázár János

As is well known, Lázár held a series of nationwide “Lázár Info” meetings, at which anyone could put questions to him freely. In practice, however, the events were carefully organised, with a loyal Fidesz core always placed in the audience to help maintain the desired atmosphere.

The reasons for defeat are being examined without taboos

The party leadership is now seeking the views of Fidesz members and local organisations. Members may complete a confidential internal questionnaire covering a wide range of issues, from the reasons for the defeat to the possibility of establishing an entirely new party.

With former President Katalin Novák: her incomprehensible decision contributed a lot to Orbán’s downfall. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

Among the potential explanations listed are that Fidesz became detached from everyday reality and from people’s concerns, and that voters grew dissatisfied as a result of economic difficulties. The questionnaire also raises the possibility that the party’s moral credibility was weakened by the presidential pardon scandal, the Szőlő Street affair and the intelligence scandal brought to light by Captain Bence Szabó.

Members are also asked whether voters simply failed to believe the excessively negative campaign, whether public money was handled irresponsibly, or whether the Tisza Party’s campaign and programme were simply more effective.

Could Fidesz cease to exist?

The questions go beyond explaining the defeat. The party is also examining how its internal communications and political style should change, Blikk reports. Respondents are asked about the need for a more direct, modern and positive tone, as well as what kind of opposition politics they expect from party members: a hard-line, combative approach or more professional and constructive criticism.

The questions concerning the party’s future go further still. Respondents are presented with options including a complete overhaul and rejuvenation of Fidesz, the creation of a new right-wing movement and, in the most radical scenario, the dissolution of Fidesz followed by the establishment of a new right-wing conservative party with a new generation of politicians.

Orbán at the Tusványos festival in Transylvania this July. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

The questionnaire also invites members to assess the suitability of several prominent politicians, including Péter Szijjártó, Gergely Gulyás, Tibor Navracsics and János Lázár, as well as Viktor Orbán. At the end, party members are given a separate opportunity to send a message directly to Orbán.

Lázár is not merely asking questions – he is preparing a report

Alongside the internal questionnaire, Lázár is personally assessing the condition of Fidesz’s organisations outside Budapest. According to Telex, he has so far concentrated mainly on counties west of the Danube and has also held talks with local constituency leaders in Szombathely.

His remit is broader still: he must map the state of the party’s entire nationwide infrastructure. This includes identifying where offices may need to be closed, gauging the mood within local organisations and determining how party members and local politicians view the defeat and Fidesz’s future.

One participant in the Szombathely meeting said Lázár had not delivered instructions, but had listened to local representatives discuss the organisational framework and renewal required for them to perform a constructive role in opposition. In addition to local leaders, a further 10 to 12 people representing the membership attended the meeting.

Decisions could come in September

Bertalan Havasi, Fidesz’s communications director, confirmed that the process was under way, but said it should not be regarded as a standalone “internal investigation”. Rather, it formed part of a comprehensive assessment of the party’s organisational, infrastructural and personnel position. Lázár had been given the mandate by the party chairman and the presidium, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

Bertalan Havasi delivering a speech on 9 July. Screenshot: Hír TV/YouTube

The report is due to be completed by September. Fidesz’s presidium will then assess the findings and, according to the announcement, take the necessary organisational, personnel and structural decisions. Havasi said the aim was to create a “clear, unified, decisive and consistent” Fidesz capable of preparing to confront Péter Magyar’s political movement from opposition.

If you missed: New President Baka could stand up firmly to PM Magyar – so why is the opposition attacking him so viciously?

In other words, the current process does not yet justify the conclusion that Fidesz is definitely preparing for a complete transformation. What is clear, however, is that after the electoral defeat the party leadership is examining its operations, communications, local organisations, personnel and future political direction all at once. The questionnaire nevertheless shows that even the most radical options for change are now being considered by the presidium.

Blikk cites the latest Medián poll, according to which Fidesz stands at 19 per cent among the entire population, 22 per cent among those who know how they would vote and 23 per cent among decided voters. The party, which once governed with a two-thirds majority, is now at its weakest level in years.

Medián was the polling organisation that accurately predicted the final results of the April election. Before the vote, prominent figures in the Orbán government responded to its surveys with attacks and attempts to cast doubt on the organisation’s professional integrity.

World.title: PM Magyar: Orbán government built ‘system to siphon off public funds’, talks about mafia
World.content:
Prime Minister Peter Magyar on Tuesday accused the previous Orbán government of having built “a system to siphon off public funds”.

PM Magyar: pseudo-civil groups linked to the Orbán government

In a video posted on Facebook, Magyar said that under the previous government, while “genuine” civil society groups had often had to compete for grants worth “only a few hundred thousand or million forints”, a world of “pseudo-civil” groups had emerged alongside them.

To illustrate this, the government has created a searchable map and database at atlathato.kormany.hu, tracking where grants intended for civil groups were allocated between 2022 and 2026, Magyar said. “Now, the past five years of grants to both genuine and pseudo-civil groups are public, allowing the public to trace the flow of some 400 billion forints [EUR 1.1bn]“, he said.

Magyar said that data on some 20,000 organisations can be viewed “constituency by constituency, town by town, organisation by organisation”. He cited the Lajos Batthyány Foundation as an example, which received around 65 billion forints in public funding during the period under review. “They financed Megafon, amongst other things,” Magyar added.

Suspicious funds to the top politicians

The Mathias Corvinus Foundation received 52 billion forints in public funds, the Land of the Future Generation Foundation, linked to János Lázár, the former construction and transport minister, received around 27 billion forints, the Blue Planet Climate Protection Foundation, linked to former President János Áder, received around 24 billion forints, Magyar said. The Kommentár Foundation in Veszprém received approximately 22 billion forints, and the Népfőiskola Foundation, linked to Fidesz deputy leader Sándor Lezsák, got approximately 6 billion forints, he added.

The faces of Fidesz during the April campaign. Photo: Facebook/Lázár János

In Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg County, former local Fidesz figures received grants of 50, 100, 150, or even 250 million forints for their “notoriously” own organisations, Magyar said. Some “front organisations” siphoned off grants intended for local civil society work and organised political events for local Fidesz-KDNP candidates, while others used public funds to publish campaign materials, party newspapers and leaflets, he added.

In one case, he said, a “pseudo-civil organisation” even nominated a candidate in an election while receiving state funds meant for “genuine” civil groups.

A mafia-like system

“This is the story of a mafia-like system in which, with one hand, the state gave public funds to the civil society sector linked to those in power, while with the other hand it attacked, stigmatised and turned genuine, independent civil society into an enemy,” Magyar said.

If you missed: PM Magyar’s stern message to richest Hungarian Lőrinc Mészáros over scheme to aid very poor, but high-achieving students

“Public funds do not belong to Fidesz, nor to any minister, nor to any lawmaker, but to the Hungarian people,” the prime minister said.

“Fidesz built this system over 16 years, and we are exposing it step by step and dismantling it brick by brick,” he said, adding that they were building “a country where civil society is truly civil society, and public funds are genuinely public funds.”

Magyar called on the “pseudo-civil” groups and those who “grew rich on billions from taxpayers” to “return the unjustly and undeservedly received funds immediately”. He warned that those who misused public funds would not escape the consequences.

World.title: Latest ranking: four Hungarian universities among the world’s best
World.content:
Four Hungarian universities have secured places among the top 1,000 universities globally, according to fresh results from one of the most influential international rankings of world-class universities. In the 2026 Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) and the University of Szeged emerged as Hungary’s joint highest-ranked establishments, both finishing in the 501–600 band.

Hungarian universities slip in Chinese-led ranking

Semmelweis University was placed in the 701–800 group, while the Budapest University of Technology and Economics (BME) fell into the 901–1,000 bracket. Compared with last year’s standings, the University of Szeged dropped one band, as did both Semmelweis and BME; ELTE’s position remained unchanged, which under the circumstances counts as a modest success.

It is worth noting that the ARWU does not primarily measure teaching quality or student satisfaction. Compiled by ShanghaiRanking Consultancy, the list focuses instead on universities’ performance in international scientific research.

The compilers analyse roughly 2,500 institutions, but publish results only for the top 1,000. Considerable weight is given to factors including the number of Nobel laureates and Fields medallists affiliated with each university, the count of highly cited researchers, and papers published in Nature and Science. Studies indexed in major international scientific databases and overall institutional research output are also taken into account, eduline.hu wrote.

American and British universities dominate the elite

US universities continue to dominate the global elite. Harvard University retained first place, followed by Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The top five was completed by the University of Cambridge and the University of California, Berkeley. Within the top ten, alongside further American institutions, Oxford and Columbia University in London also featured.

The main building of the Budapest University of Technology and Economics. Photo: FB/BME

If you missed: Top Hungarian university’s vice-rector resigns after exam scandal that ended in lecturer’s dismissal

Consequently, the Hungarian universities’ placements chiefly reflect their standing in research and scientific output on the international stage, and do not in themselves imply that these institutions offer uniformly high standards across all fields of study.

Incidentally, the ranking was first published in 2003 and, since 2009, has been produced by ShanghaiRanking Consultancy, an organisation independent of governments and universities.

World.title: Good news for homebuyers and students: vast student city and residential district could rise on Budapest’s derelict waterfront
World.content:
Transport Minister Dávid Vitézy was unequivocal at a press conference yesterday: the Tisza government wants to tackle not only the shortage of student accommodation, but also the housing crisis. While a number of measures have already been outlined in the latter area, there has been a significant shift in the approach to the former. Whereas previous Orbán governments had envisaged some form of Chinese university project for Budapest, Péter Magyar’s administration now wants to revive and deliver plans for a student city and a new residential district on the very same site.

Major development in Budapest’s brownfield zone

“We will review the old plans, but the objective remains unchanged: to create a high-quality mixed residential and student-accommodation district that will also help ease Budapest’s housing crisis,” Dávid Vitézy wrote in a Facebook post yesterday.

Vitézy was also closely involved in plans for the creation of a 36-hectare park in northern Csepel in the early 2020s, when he was head of the Budapest Development Centre.

The original Snøhetta plan for the entire project: the park in North Csepel in the left hand side, the athletics stadium in the middle (completed) and the student city in the right hand side. Photo: Karácsony Gergely / Facebook

The original project envisaged three main elements in the derelict brownfield areas of northern Csepel and neighbouring Ferencváros: a stadium and associated training pitches for the 2023 World Athletics Championships; a student city; and a vast public park. The stadium was built and opened to the public at the end of 2024.

The scheme could also have included the Albertfalva bridge across the Danube, together with a counterpart over the smaller branch of the river, potentially carrying a tram service.

Of those three elements, however, only the artist’s impressions have survived. According to Vitézy, master plans had also been completed for the student city, but the previous government shelved them after 2021 because it preferred to allocate the site to China’s Fudan University, which intended to develop a European campus there.

Orbán government’s Chinese project collapses

The proposal met fierce opposition from local residents and successful resistance from the municipalities concerned. One of the more colourful side effects was the naming of nearby streets after causes such as Hong Kong’s freedom and the Dalai Lama.

Gergely Karácsony, Budapest’s mayor, claimed at the time that the government had initially presented plans under which the student city and Fudan University could be built side by side. It later emerged, he said, that the Chinese university’s campus would in fact occupy the site intended for student accommodation.

Karácsony therefore argued that the Fudan project would effectively have displaced the original student city.

Acute need for modern student accommodation

The student-city project was intended to create a new district aimed primarily at addressing university students’ housing problems. Student residences would have formed the centrepiece of the development, with the aim of providing large numbers of affordable homes for those in higher education.

The project would not simply have involved putting up a handful of halls of residence. It represented a broader urban-development vision, combining accommodation with the infrastructure and services required for a functioning neighbourhood.

If you missed: The surprising reasons Viktor Orbán’s father was fined millions over his castle project

According to surveys, Budapest is currently short of 34,000 student-accommodation places. A substantial proportion of the existing halls leave much to be desired, yet demand is still three times greater than supply. The shortage is also pushing up property prices and rents.

https://www.facebook.com/snohetta

Vitézy said yesterday that construction could soon begin on the vast site, with plans for both a residential district and a student city. He did not provide figures for the number of homes or student places to be built, nor did he set out what other facilities might be included.

He said only that the fundamental objectives remained the same, but that the previous master plan would need to be revised.

World.title: Photos – Miss Balaton 2026 crowned: 21-year-old Hungarian woman is the most beautiful
World.content:
The winner of Miss Balaton 2026 has been announced: Emőke Antal, a 21-year-old contestant from Satu Mare (Szatmárnémeti), was crowned on Saturday evening in Balatonfüred. She will hold the Miss Balaton title for the coming year and represent the lake region at various public events.

Finalists and runners-up

Boglárka Vasvári finished as first runner-up (first lady-in-waiting), while Larina Vittmann took second runner-up (second lady-in-waiting). The final ranking was decided by a professional jury composed of public figures and industry experts after the contestants appeared in several rounds.

Source: Miss Balaton 2026

The jury

The judging panel included former beauty queen Ágnes Dobó, ex-national water polo player Gábor Hegedűs, Krisztina Maróy, editor-in-chief of GLAMOUR, and model Andrea Rábaközi, with photographer Pál Nánási serving as jury president. The evening was hosted by Tímea Gelencsér and Eszter Iszak.

The 21-year-old winner. Source: Miss Balaton 2026

Road to the final

This year’s competition followed a lengthy selection process: from the initial applicants, 60 contestants advanced, then 24, before the final 12 were chosen for the grand finale. The finalists prepared in a photo camp at the end of July and a training camp in August ahead of the final.

Source: Miss Balaton 2026

About the winner

Emőke Antal, who entered the final with contestant number 12 and often appeared last in the line-up, said she wanted to prove to herself that she could succeed regardless of her background or coming from a small town. Originally from Transylvania, she is currently studying management at Babeș-Bolyai University in Cluj-Napoca/Kolozsvár and hopes to open a modelling school after graduation. The crown was passed to her by the reigning 2024 queen, Virág Bábel.

World.title: Sick Hungarian boy placed for adoption in US despite Hungarian foster parents’ bid – video
World.content:
Hungarian foster parents who cared for a seriously ill six-year-old boy say they cannot understand why the country’s child protection authorities placed him for adoption in the United States – and they continue to fight for his return.

Tibike, who does not speak English, was handed over to American adoptive parents by Hungary’s child welfare system despite congenital health problems and multiple heart operations. His Hungarian foster family have been campaigning for him ever since, and the case has now been raised in the National Assembly. Officials cite an unusual provision of Hungarian law, but questions remain over whether sending the child to Texas – where he must be protected from excessive sunlight – was truly in his best interests.

Foster parents hoped to adopt the boy

While his Hungarian foster parents are still pursuing legal avenues to keep him, all indications suggest that Tibike has already been adopted by an American family. Yet numerous unresolved questions surround the case of the six-year-old, who lives with severe health complications.

Tibike with his Hungarian foster parents. Photo: Facebook/Füssy Angéla újságíró

Tibike had been living with Tamás Horváth and his wife for more than a year. Previously raised in a children’s home, he gradually formed a close bond with the couple, who wished to adopt him. Their application was rejected, however, on the grounds that the age difference between the child and at least one adoptive parent exceeded the legal limit by 15 months. They requested an individual assessment, but to no avail.

Under Hungarian law, the age gap between an adopted child and at least one adoptive parent may not exceed 50 years if the child is over three (or 45 years if younger). In the meantime, Tibike was placed on the international adoption list. According to his foster parents, foreign interest in him emerged in January, and by spring introductions had begun with a Texas-based family. In June, he was taken from the foster home for a 30-day bonding period. Horváth says he left for work that morning expecting the boy to return that evening; he never came back, and the family was not even allowed to say goodbye.

Since then, the foster parents say they have received scant information about the child’s condition, and claim they have not even been formally notified that their foster-care status has been terminated. By mid-July, however, the former guardian informed Dávid Dócs, an MP and deputy chairman of the Mi Hazánk party, that the adoption had gone through and that his own guardianship had ended.

Boy may already be in America

All this raises particular concerns because the Hungarian family’s adoption request was only formally rejected on 22 July. In other words, while the foster parents’ legal battle was still under way, the American adoption may already have been completed.

Tibike has undergone three heart surgeries and, owing to a genetic disorder, must be carefully shielded from sunlight. His foster parents therefore question what medical and psychological assessments preceded the decision. Was the boy’s strong attachment to his Hungarian family properly evaluated? Was due consideration given to the fact that he would be moved into a different linguistic and cultural environment, where his new parents do not speak Hungarian? And on what basis was Texas deemed suitable for a child in such a fragile state of health?

The Directorate-General for Social and Child Protection Services maintains that such decisions are the result of a lengthy process involving multiple specialists. It says Tibike’s health, attachments, views and long-term interests were all weighed, and that the boy is now safe and developing well in his new family.

The question, then, is not merely why Tibike was made available for adoption abroad. It is also how this could happen so swiftly, when a Hungarian family had already been raising him as their own for more than a year and wished to adopt him.

British couple leave Hungary after authorities blocked adoption of newborn baby

Horváth has since resigned from his role in child protection, and the family is continuing its fight with the help of a family-law solicitor. Dávid Dócs raised the matter in Parliament, but received no answer from the Government at the time.

Child welfare service: boy is developing well in Texas

In an earlier response, the National Child Protection Specialist Service (OGYSZ) clarified that numerous factors are taken into account in adoption cases. According to that reply, the boy’s “integration is progressing favourably; he has undergone significant physical development, the bodily symptoms that previously caused problems have disappeared, he is increasingly relaxed in his new family, and several symptoms that previously indicated internal tension have eased or vanished. These are important signs that he is gradually feeling safe in his new environment.”

The OGYSZ press officer said the child’s attachments were developing well, and that breaking them and removing him again would cause further losses and trauma. On that basis, the institution does not expect to reach a different decision.

World.title: Polish bus tragedy: expert reveals how and why it happened – and how such crashes can be survived
World.content:
Twelve people died and 47 were injured in the Polish bus tragedy on the M3 motorway near Mezőkeresztes late last Sunday night. The bus, carrying pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland, left the carriageway, plunged into a drainage ditch and overturned. Police preliminarily suspect the driver fell asleep at the wheel. A forensic vehicle expert has now outlined how long the driver may have been unconscious, how the crash unfolded and what might prevent similar tragedies in future.

Polish bus tragedy: how a few seconds proved fatal

Based on evidence at the scene, the driver appears to have lost alertness for only a matter of seconds. Sándor Boncsér, a court-certified automotive engineering expert, told Telex that as little as two to four seconds of micro-sleep could have been enough to cause the catastrophe. At roughly 100km/h, the 24-tonne vehicle would have travelled more than 100 metres in four seconds with no one at the controls. If cruise control was engaged, the speed would barely have dropped before the driver regained consciousness.

Because motorways are cambered slightly to shed rainwater, the bus drifted gradually to the right after the driver nodded off. The Scania’s right-hand wheels left the tarmac, crossed the hard shoulder and mounted the embankment. On the steep slope, traction on the right-side wheels was lost, making it virtually impossible to steer the bus back onto the road.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

The absence of a continuous crash barrier on this stretch meant there was nothing to arrest the vehicle’s departure from the carriageway. On the steep embankment, the bus’s centre of gravity shifted laterally, causing it to roll over. The expert added that the roof structure may not have been designed to absorb the mass and kinetic energy involved, contributing to the severity of the crash.

Who stands the best chance of survival?

Seat-belt use significantly affects survival odds. On Tempo 100-rated coaches, motorway regulations require all passengers to wear seat belts, but with 50–60 travellers on board, the driver cannot realistically check who has unbuckled during the journey. Reports that several passengers were thrown from the bus suggest many were not restrained.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

How to prevent future tragedies

The most critical factor remains driver alertness. EU rules strictly govern driving and rest periods, although more flexible provisions for tourist-coach drivers have applied since 2024. Technology can also help: modern coaches may be fitted with systems that monitor fatigue, eye movement and steering patterns, alongside lane-departure warnings, active lane-keeping and emergency-brake assist.

Yet technology alone cannot eliminate risk. European Commission data suggest driver fatigue contributes to 15–20 per cent of road accidents. Hungary’s public road authority recorded 716 crashes between early 2020 and March 2026 in which the driver was confirmed to have fallen asleep.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

If you missed our previous article concerning the tragedy: ‘People were shouting, trapped beneath the seats’ – exclusive interview, video and latest developments in Polish bus crash

What the driver now faces

The driver’s criminal liability has not yet been determined. Authorities must examine tachograph data, driving and rest periods, speed records and any possible mechanical faults. If convicted of causing a mass-casualty traffic accident resulting in death, he could face two to eight years’ imprisonment, plus fines and a multi-year driving ban. Sentencing will take into account his prior record and whether he breached traffic regulations.

The tragedy’s starkest lesson is that, with a vehicle weighing dozens of tonnes, even a few seconds’ loss of attention can prove fatal. By the time a driver realises the coach has left the road, its motion may already be irreversible.

‘It happened in seconds’: Another survivor reveals horror of deadly Polish bus crash on Hungary’s motorway

World.title: Key deal secured for new Danube bridge at Mohács – new photos
World.content:
Construction company Duna Aszfalt has agreed to refund the state HUF 59bn of an advance payment for a bridge it is building across the Danube at Mohács (Southwest Hungary), Transportation and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy said in a post on Facebook on Monday.

New deal struck concerning the new Danube bridge

Vitézy noted that János Lázár, the head of the transportation portfolio under the former Fidesz-KDNP government, had decided to raise the advance payment rate for the project from 20pc to 98pc just two days ahead of the election in April.

Vitézy said the government was also seeking to recover HUF 76bn in additional costs related to a decision taken by Lázár to build a 20km expressway connecting to the bridge, even though traffic volume was not expected to require the link for 25 years or more.

Public interest in the last place

He called the bridge project a “typical NER story“, using a Hungarian acronym referring to companies that benefitted from big state contracts under the Fidesz-KDNP government: “All other interests superseded those of the public”.

He added that the government would not shelve the bridge project as it could not be reversed. In a separate statement on Monday, Duna Aszfalt confirmed it would refund the advance payment and said future payments for the project would take place on a monthly basis, linked to milestones.

World.title: British investor Ghai Sant Ram's HORIZON CITY project in northern Bucharest secures EUR 36 mln financing from Libra Bank
World.content:
HORIZON CITY, the residential project developed by British investor Ghai Sant Ram in northern Bucharest, has secured EUR 36.5 million in financing from Libra Internet Bank. The total investment exceeds EUR 130 million.

The financing provides the necessary resources for the building process independently of the pace at which advance payments are collected from buyers under pre-sale agreements. As such, it will allow for the acceleration of construction works, with full project completion targeted for the first half of 2027, six months earlier than initially announced, according to a press release.

“For buyers, this financial structure means greater predictability and security regarding the accelerated progress of the project,” said Cătălin Apetri, CEO and Founder of CGA Home Consulting and Development Director for Romania for investor Ghai Sant Ram.

HORIZON CITY is being developed on Pipera Boulevard, on a 23,000-square-metre site, and comprises 699 residential units arranged across eight stairwells and two development phases. The project provides 926 parking spaces, including 900 underground and 26 above ground.

“We are entering an important stage of the project, in which the focus is increasingly shifting to installations, partitions and finishes. The financing we have secured allows us to plan the next stages very clearly, accelerate works wherever possible,” said Cristian Stanciu, CEO of the HORIZON CITY project.

As construction progresses, the developer has finalized discussions with third parties and suppliers for the main categories of finishes and equipment to be integrated into HORIZON CITY.

The acceleration of HORIZON CITY is taking place in parallel with the expansion of British investor Ghai Sant Ram’s portfolio in Romania. Recently, through Ghai Family Holding, he acquired from businessman George Becali a plot of approximately 30,000 square metres located near Pipera Plaza. The transaction was valued at approximately EUR 14.3 million, and the land was acquired together with the permit for the development of a large-scale real estate project.

With 1,188 apartments at IVORY RESIDENCE, 699 units at HORIZON CITY, and approximately 650 homes planned in the recently acquired new project, the investor’s residential portfolio in Romania exceeds 2,500 units.

World.title: SAI Globinvest launches ETF replicating Bucharest Stock Exchange’s reference BET-XT index
World.content:
Romanian investment management company SAI Globinvest listed its second ETF on the Regulated Market of the Bucharest Stock Exchange on Tuesday, August 18. The ETF, listed under the ticker symbol GIBXTETF, aims to fully replicate the structure of BVB's reference index (BET-XT).

Launched by BVB in 2008, BET-XT is a price index that tracks the performance of the 30 most traded Romanian companies on the BVB Regulated Market. Having a broader composition than the benchmark BET index, it offers a wider perspective on the evolution of the Romanian capital market.

The BET-XT index components include representative companies from key sectors of the Romanian economy, such as financial, energy, pharmaceutical, industrial, and utilities. The total market capitalization of all Romanian companies included in the BET-XT index stands at approximately RON 438 billion, representing 60% of the main segment's total market capitalization, which exceeded RON 724 billion at the end of the day on August 17.

In terms of yield, from its launch to date, BET-XT displays a 340% increase. At the same time, the first half of 2026 recorded the index's best H1 performance since its launch.

Also in 2026, the BET-XT index surpassed the 3,000-point threshold for the first time, reaching 3.078,66 points following the trading session on August 17. Since the beginning of the year, BET-XT has appreciated by 46%.

"With the launch of Globinvest's second ETF, we reach the milestone of 10 ETFs available for trading on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. This is a confirmation of our market's maturity and the democratization of investing through ETFs," said Radu Hanga, President of the Bucharest Stock Exchange.

SAI Globinvest is a Romanian investment management company with 30 years of experience, founded in Cluj-Napoca. Within 16 months, Globinvest has brought two ETF financial instruments to BVB, the first being Globinvest Energy & Financials ETF, launched in April 2025, which tracks the performance of the BET-EF sector index and offered investors a maximum return of over 125% since launch.

Net assets of the investment funds managed by SAI Globinvest total approximately RON 535 million. The initial assets of the GIBXTETF ETF amount to RON 4.1 million. The ETF benefits from liquidity provider (market maker) services provided by TradeVille, which also handled the admission of the ETF fund units under the ticker symbol GIBXTETF to the BVB Regulated Market.

World.title: Romania’s drone production capacities to rapidly increase in coming years, minister says
World.content:
Romania’s drone production capacity will increase rapidly in the coming years thanks to private companies and public initiatives, said interim economy minister Irineu Darău on Monday, August 17, in an interview with Euronews Romania.

The increase will be noticeable beginning with 2027, the minister said, thanks to the funds made available through the SAFE Act. Local drone production may also benefit from partnerships with Ukrainian companies.

“There are private companies that are starting to innovate a lot in this field and already have foreign partners. I am convinced that all these joint efforts, private and public, will have an effect without a delay,” the official said.

Darău noted that Romania has recently shot down drones that illegally crossed its airspace. While this has been done by military airplanes, the country will soon benefit from a drone-based defense industry.

“We have entered an accelerated phase of innovation, and I am confident that very soon we will have a defense industry also based on drones that will help us. Firmly within the horizon of 2027, our domestic production capacities will increase rapidly,” Irineu Darău said.

Drones have come to dominate the battlefield in Ukraine and have even been used by Iran in its asymmetric conflict with the United States and Israel. Russia and Ukraine have both relied on drones for close- but also long-range strikes on each other.

The number of drone attacks recorded on Ukrainian territory, near the border with Romania, has exceeded 110 since the beginning of the war. In 39 cases, Russian drones were reported to have entered Romanian airspace, including the drone shot down on August 16 in Galați County, according to a Ministry of National Defense statistic consulted by News.ro.

Since the beginning of this year, authorities have recorded 54 instances of attacks near Romania’s border. In 42 of these cases, aircraft from the Air Policing Combat Service were scrambled to monitor and verify the air situation. In approximately 50 cases, drones or drone fragments were identified on Romanian territory.

The incidents took place against the backdrop of an unprecedented intensification, during that period, of drone attacks carried out by Russia against targets in southern Ukraine. The main targets were Ukrainian Danube ports, located near the Romanian border and the Danube Delta.

The attacks also involved swarm launches, which explains the large number of drones detected by Romanian radars near national airspace. Some aircraft were intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses, and their fragments reached Romania or the waters of the Black Sea.

(Photo source: Irineu Darău on Facebook)

World.title: Romania’s Enescu Competition introduces play & conduct format for 2026 semifinals
World.content:
Semifinalists in the cello, violin, and piano sections of the 2026 George Enescu International Competition will perform as both soloists and orchestra leaders in a new “play & conduct” format. Introduced for the first time in the competition’s history, the conductor-free semifinals will take place at the Romanian Athenaeum in Bucharest in September.

The cello semifinal is scheduled for September 5, followed by the violin competition on September 11 and the piano event on September 17. Six contestants from each instrumental section will advance to this stage.

Each semifinal will be divided into two parts. First, at 10 a.m., the contestants will perform works by Romanian composer George Enescu, with free public admission.

Then, the play & conduct round will begin at 4 p.m. and require a ticket. During this stage, each contestant will perform as a soloist with the Radio Chamber Orchestra while simultaneously providing the ensemble’s artistic direction without a conductor.

The musicians will have to communicate their interpretation to the orchestra through gestures, eye contact, breathing, and movement while performing their own parts, the organizers said. They will be assessed on their solo performance, musical communication, and ability to lead the ensemble toward a coherent interpretation.

Cello semifinalists will perform Enescu’s Cello Sonata No. 2 in C Major, Op. 26 during the first part of the competition. For the play & conduct round, they will choose one of Joseph Haydn’s two cello concertos.

The violin contestants will perform either Enescu’s Violin Sonata No. 2 in F Minor, Op. 6 or Violin Sonata No. 3 in A Minor, Op. 25, “in Romanian folk character.” They will then perform and lead the orchestra in one of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s Violin Concertos Nos. 3, 4 or 5.

Piano semifinalists will select one of three works by Enescu: Suite No. 2 in D Major, Op. 10, Piano Sonata No. 1 in F-sharp Minor, Op. 24 or Piano Sonata No. 3 in D Major, Op. 24. Their play & conduct repertoire will consist of Mozart’s Piano Concertos Nos. 20, 21 or 23.

The Radio Chamber Orchestra will perform with guest concertmasters Adrian Iliescu for the cello semifinal, Deborah Nemțanu for the violin event, and Sebastian Câșleanu for the piano section.

Up to 50 contestants can be admitted to the first stage of each instrumental section. Twelve will advance to the second round, six to the semifinals, and three to the final.

Tickets for the afternoon sessions are available through Eventim and at Cărturești and Humanitas bookstores. Students, pupils, and teachers from music schools and universities can attend free of charge with valid identification, subject to availability. People with disabilities and their companions are also eligible for free admission, subject to available seats.

The complete program of the 2026 George Enescu International Competition is available on the competition’s official website.
